newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-BRITISH CLUBS HUMILIATED IN AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BRITISH CLUBS HUMILIATED IN AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Australian rugby league clubs humiliated British rivals on Sunday, prompting former British international Andy Gregory to warn about a decline in playing standards.
Four visiting European Super League teams were thrashed by Australian opponents in the World Club Challenge competition at the weekend.
The Salford coach watched his side sink to a 50-8 defeat against Adelaide Rams on Sunday in the inaugural competition involving Super League teams in Europe and Australia.
"We cannot compete with the Australians in club competition," Gregory said.
"I could try to kid myself and kid the British public by saying everything is going great in the European Super League but it's not.
"I believe the winners of this competition will come from Australia. The Australian Super League is by far superior to the European league," he added.

Canberra highlighted the gulf in class by thrashing Halifax 70-6 in an embarrassingly one-sided match at Bruce Stadium on Sunday. Fullback Ken Nagas scored six of his side's 13 tries as the Raiders recorded the highest points total in their history.
In other matches in Australia this weekend, North Queensland beat Leeds 42-20, while Brisbane thrashed London Broncos 42-22.
Gregory said Great Britain were losing touch with the Australians after nearly matching them at test level in the early 1990s.
